title: Zenith sidepanel pathways prototype for multi-tenant context switching
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Replace the current monolithic left rail with a compact, role-aware sidepanel that reduces time-to-target for engineers and product teams navigating dashboards, rollouts, and cost views. Scope: information architecture mapping, low-fi and high-fi prototypes, route taxonomy, compact vs expanded states, quick-switch modal, telemetry hooks for measuring time-to-target, and acceptance criteria for rollouts UX. Success metrics: median time to open a target dashboard <2.5s, 80%+ task success in prototype usability tests for workspace switching, 10% reduction in navigation-related support tickets after rollout. Key constraints: must preserve existing deep links for third-party integrations, support multi-tenant workspace hierarchy, and maintain accessibility (keyboard-first) and screen-reader semantics.
design_decisions: Adopt a compact left sidepanel by default with progressive expansion on hover or explicit toggle to preserve screen real-estate for dashboards and logs.

Introduce a 3-tier route taxonomy: Global (Account/Settings/Billing), Workspace (Projects/Models/Dedicated), and Contextual (Active run/dashboard/trace). This reduces route duplication and clarifies navigation affordances.
Add a quick-switch keyboard-driven modal (Cmd/Ctrl+K) that surfaces pinned routes, recent pages, and workspace switcher with fuzzy search to optimize fast path navigation.
Expose rollout controls inline on rollout-related routes: compact banner with quick rollback and canary percentage preview to reduce task friction for SREs and PMs.
Surface a micro-cost tile in the sidepanel that shows per-route cost delta for the last 24h and links to the detailed cost view for high-affinity cost troubleshooting.
Keep deep-link compatibility: maintain canonical route names and query params. Router migration will map old paths to new slugs via a middleware layer in the app shell.
Role-aware ordering: developer, infra, and billing personas see reordered primary nav items by default with an option to pin personal preferences.
Accessibility: full keyboard navigation, aria-expanded semantics for grouped routes, and focus management for workspace switches and modals.
Telemetry: instrument nav click streams, quick-switch use, and time-to-first-paint for route transitions to validate hypotheses.

acceptance_criteria: Quick-switch modal opens within 150ms on cold start in Hosted Console and <250ms in Dedicated with cold GPU allocation.
Keyboard-only users can access every primary route and switch workspace without a mouse; validated in manual accessibility pass.
Canary rollout shows no >5% regression in route render time and no increase in error-rate for navigation-related endpoints.
Cost micro-tile matches backend per-route cost delta within 3% margin and links to detailed cost page.
Deep-links from existing external dashboards resolve to correct new routes via middleware for 100% of known patterns in the migration mapping table.
